title: Stability-first activation roadmap
content:
Purpose:
A compact, actionable roadmap + KPI tracker focused on a stability-first activation strategy for new feature launches (particularly model-serving and routing changes). This doc is a single-pane working sheet for product-ops, SRE, serving runtime, and solutions engineering to align canary gating criteria, traffic ramps, and rollback triggers.

Quick summary of approach:
- Prioritize safety & availability over rapid adoption: small staged ramps with capacity floors and automatic fallbacks.
- Gate on both infrastructure signals (latency, error rate, GPU saturation) and quality signals (regression rate vs baseline evals, user-facing errors).
- Use short, observable ramps (15–120m windows) with explicit checkpoint owners and automated rollback hooks.

Core KPI table (single-row per signal):
KPI | Target / Gate | Owner | Measurement cadence | Accept threshold | Action on breach
- 95th-ile latency (inference) | <= 300ms | Connor Blake | 1m | > 350ms sustained 3m | Pause traffic + notify SRE
- Error rate (5xx from runtime) | <= 0.5% | Diego Rivera | 1m | > 1.5% sustained 2m | Rollback to prior model variant
- Quality regression (eval set) | <= 1.0% delta | Maya Singh | 30m (sampled) | > 2.5% | Stop ramp, flag ML lead
- Token cost per 1k | <= $0.95 | Product-ops | 60m | > $1.30 | Hold ramp, evaluate quantization config
- Prefix cache hit ratio | >= 40% | Serving runtime | 5m | < 20% | Review batching/caching config
- Customer-facing errors (SLA breaches) | 0 incidents | Customer Success | real-time | 1 incident | Immediate rollback and incident bridge

Traffic ramp schedule (template)
- Canary 1: 0.5% global traffic for 30m (owner: Release on-call)
  - Goals: no infra breaches, eval regression <= 1% over sampled traffic
- Canary 2: 2% for 60m (owner: Release on-call + SRE)
  - Add: load profile with P95 <= 300ms, GPU util < 70% sustained
- Ramp 1: 10% for 120m (owner: Product-ops lead)
- Ramp 2: 33% for 4h (owner: Product PM)
- Global: 100% (post-checklist clear)

Canary gating checklist (pre-canary gates must be green)
- [ ] Model version pinned and verified in model catalog (PR linked)
- [ ] Load test baseline run with synthetic traffic (Jira PROJ-812: load-test-branch)
- [ ] Rollback playbook published in playbook repo (GitHub PR 221)
- [ ] SLO burn rate guardrails configured (ops console)
- [ ] Health checks (liveness/probe) pass on all nodes
- [ ] Alert routing to #launch-control and on-call paging configured
- [ ] Key stakeholders present for canary window (SRE, ML lead, Product, Solutions Eng)

Automatic rollback triggers (configurable)
- Any single threshold breach labeled as 'automatic rollback' will trigger immediate traffic re-route to fallback model variant and create an incident:
  - error rate > 3% for 1 minute
  - P95 latency > 500ms for 2 minutes
  - GPU OOM or node crash cluster-wide
  - Quality regression > 5% on production-sampled evals

Manual pause conditions (requires assessment, not auto-rollback)
- Steady incremental rise in tail latency with no clear infra cause
- Intermittent user-facing hallucination patterns flagged by QA team
- Unexpected cost increase not explained by traffic pattern

Operations playbook (what happens during a breach)
1) Alert fires -> SRE on-call pages -> owner acknowledges within 5m
2) Owner runs immediate triage checklist: logs + p95/throughput + GPU metrics
3) If auto-rollback criteria met -> execute rollback runbook (traffic-switch + deploy previous variant)
4) If manual pause condition -> pause next ramp, open bridge for 30m triage, collect debug traces
5) Post-incident: blameless postmortem in Confluence and follow-up Jira for fixes

Monitoring & dashboards to have live during ramps
- Per-model P50/P90/P95 latency trend (1m/5m windows)
- Error waterfall (client error vs server error vs model rejection)
- GPU node saturation + OOM events
- Cost estimator per-1k tokens with rolling window
- Sampled user queries + model outputs for spot QA checks

Escalation path (owners)
- Release on-call (first responder) -> SRE lead -> ML infra -> Product PM -> CTO if incident severity P0

Pre-launch quick wins (to reduce instability risk)
- Pre-warm KV caches before canary traffic window to improve cache hit ratio
- Apply conservative batching ceilings during canary windows to maintain latency SLOs
- Use a quantized fallback variant with known cost/latency profile as automatic fallback

Open questions / unresolved items
- Decide final sample size and eval frequency for "production-sampled evals" (proposed: 1 in 500 live requests)
- Confirm retention window for trace logs for root-cause analysis (30d vs 90d)
- Add an observable for "unexpected semantic regression" (UX signal) — need QA pattern library

Next steps (owners & immediate actions)
- Diego: finish load test job and attach results to JIRA PROJ-812 (due 2026-03-15)
- Connor: add automatic rollback hook to routing service and verify in staging (due 2026-03-10)
- Maya: assemble eval sample harness and share evaluation notebook (due 2026-03-11)
- Asha: schedule readiness review + dry run with SRE (calendar invite sent)

Notes to self (working doc style)
- Keep ramp windows conservative for first two quarters of large model changes.
- Capture any manual interventions during ramps as a single timeline entry in Confluence (PRODOPS-STAB-3).
- This sheet is intentionally compact — handoff to formal launch playbook after a successful dry run.

Attachments / quick links:
- Load test results: linked_artifacts JIRA PROJ-812
- Rollback runbook: GitHub PR 221
- Readiness review notes: confluence PRODOPS-STAB-3

If anything is missing or you want a separate per-customer variant checklist, flag in #launch-control and I will fork a specialized copy.
